name: PRDGenie WF0 - LLM Call
_comment_active: Must be active even though it has no trigger of its own: n8n refuses to run an inactive workflow as a subworkflow ('Workflow is not active and cannot be executed').

parameters.content:
## WF0 — the only door to a model

**This is the only workflow that holds a provider credential.** Every other workflow calls it as a subworkflow. That is what makes cost logging unbypassable: there is no second path to a model to forget to instrument.

Input:  `{ system, user, schema, prompt_name, prompt_version, component, trace_id, doc_id }`
Output: an envelope — `ok` with parsed JSON, or `needs_review` with a reason.

It never returns a partial result and never falls back to another vendor. A park is honest; a silently different model is not.

parameters.content:
## Cost accounting

Token counts are **provider-reported**, never estimated from characters. Unit prices come from a local table, so rows are labelled `estimated` — a correction can sit beside them later instead of overwriting them (docs/traceability.md).

This write is **continue-on-failure**: observability may fail, the product may not.

googlePalmApi.name: PRDGenie judge provider — bind with bind-provider-credential.mjs

parameters.content:
## Two vendors, one door

**The grader is never the doer** (ADR 0001). The doer is OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`; the judge is Google `gemini-3.8-flash` with its thinking budget at **0**, so both sides of the project stay non-reasoning.

They share this workflow on purpose: one classifier, one cost row, one envelope. A judge with its own private path to a provider would be a second place for a key to live and a second place for a failure to be recorded differently.

**There is no fallback between them.** If Gemini is unavailable the sweep is RECORDED AS SKIPPED (E7-S5); it never quietly becomes an OpenAI opinion.

**Both nodes retry the same way, and the drill counted it: 22 calls against a refusing server produced 44 requests.** So a 5xx IS retried even though `neverError` keeps it out of the error path — the retry is a second attempt, and only the second reply is classified. Measured, not assumed (E7-S5).

## One retry, for one kind of failure

**A bad ANSWER is retried; no answer is not.** An unparseable reply may parse on the
second ask; an auth failure, an empty balance or a rate limit will not, and asking
again would spend money on a condition that cannot pass.

**Both attempts write their own `llm_calls` row.** One merged row would hide the
signal `docs/traceability.md` names: the attempt-2 rate is how a model returning
malformed JSON more often announces itself.

**Bounded at two by the attempt itself**, not by a counter somebody has to maintain:
the condition is `attempt == 1`, so a second failure parks with the reason it always
would have.
